page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-16GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks present a mixed profile due to the shared CPU allocation. The server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench with a score of 2243.0, and strong text processing capabilities at 2793.0. However, multi-core and sustained compute benchmarks are generally weak or poor. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests fall into the bottom 10%, and the Passmark CPU score of 4048.74 is in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 33.08 GB/sec, though write speeds remain average at 26.54 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high memory density relative to its shared compute resources, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, heavy CPU utilization. Tradeoffs include poor multi-threaded decompression and static web serving throughput. This configuration is best suited for lightweight database operations, text processing tasks, basic memory-cached applications, and small-scale LLM text generation using lightweight models.
